2. \(B\) is the set of people who think fuchsia is "purply".
3. \(n(A)\) is the number of people in set \(A\).
4. \(n(B)\) is the number of people in set \(B\).
5. \(n(A \cap B)\) is the number of people who think fuchsia is both "kinda pink" and "purply".

\[ 83 = 60 + n(B) - 27 \]

The radius of this sector is the slant height of the cone, which is given by $\sqrt{600^2 + (200\sqrt{7})^2} = 1000$. The circumference of the base of the cone is $2\pi \cdot 600 = 1200\pi$.

The fly starts at a point on the surface of the cone whose distance from the vertex is 125. When we unroll the cone, this point corresponds to a point on the sector that is 125 units from the center. Similarly, the fly ends at a point on the exact opposite side of the cone whose distance from the vertex is $375\sqrt{2}$. The straight-line distance between these two points on the sector is the shortest distance the fly could have crawled. The angle subtended by this chord at the center of the sector can be found by considering the arc lengths corresponding to the points on the cone.
